title: Streaming OTLP transform & router for tenant-aware redaction and sampling normalization
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a lightweight streaming OTLP transform/router service that sits between producers and tracing backends. The service will: 1) apply tenant-specific redaction rules to span attributes and resource attributes, 2) normalize sampling metadata (map head-based sampling decisions to backend-compatible flags), 3) convert or enrich spans for compatibility with Jaeger v1 and Tempo ingestion formats, and 4) provide fault-tolerant fanout with backpressure and configurable fallback (buffer-to-disk or S3). Goal: reduce incorrect PII emissions, ensure sampling semantics are preserved across fallbacks, and simplify backend wiring for multi-tenant customers.
acceptance_criteria: Can receive streaming OTLP/gRPC from service mesh and SDKs at 10k spans/sec with median processing latency < 12ms per-span at 95th percentile on our test hardware
Tenant-configurable redaction rules applied and verified via integration tests (regex and key whitelist/blacklist)
Sampling normalization documented and reflected in Console (mapping table + examples), with preserved decision when forwarded to Jaeger and Tempo
Graceful degradation: when backends are unavailable, spans are buffered with size- and time-based eviction and a fallback mechanism to object storage; no data loss for <= 5 minutes under target load
Exposes internal metrics: processed_spans_total, redacted_spans_total, sampling_mismatch_count, backend_errors, buffer_queue_depth
End-to-end tests and a canary rollout plan exist; security review completed for redaction logic and KMS integration
design_decisions: Use streaming gRPC OTLP receiver to minimize memory overhead and support continuous KV cache passing for high-QPS services
Implement rule engine using an embedded WASM evaluator to allow tenant-supplied redaction predicates without recompiling the service
Perform sampling normalization by preserving otel.trace_flags and adding a vendor_sampling attribute for backends that require it
Fanout model: primary synchronous push to backends with async retry workers and configurable fallback to S3 for durable buffering
Keep transformations idempotent and attach transformation provenance metadata to spans for debugging
